description:
Barangay San Pedro is the vibrant historic heart of Davao City, anchoring the Poblacion district with centuries-old heritage, bustling street markets, and warm Mindanaoan hospitality.

At its center stands the iconic San Pedro Cathedral, originally built in 1847 and redesigned with a distinctive sweeping concrete prow-shaped roof. Steps away lie San Pedro Square, Davao City Hall, Osmeña Park, and the Museo Dabawenyo, where visitors can explore indigenous Bagobo, Mandaya, and Kagan weaving and artifacts.

As dusk settles, San Pedro comes alive along Roxas Avenue Night Market, where charcoal-grilled tuna panga, durian delicacies, ukay-ukay stalls, and local street food bring the entire city together.

Tagum is a vibrant and bustling city located in the province of Davao del Norte, Philippines, celebrated as the Palm City of the Philippines and the Music Capital of the South.

Visitors can admire the soaring architecture of the Christ the King Cathedral—home to the largest wooden rosary in the world—and the expansive Tagum City Historical & Cultural Center. Nature lovers enjoy the lush Botanical & Eco-Park, Energy Park, and scenic Nabintad River cruises.

Just 50 minutes north of Davao City along the Pan-Philippine Highway, Tagum also serves as a convenient hub for exploring banana plantations, Davao del Norte coastal resorts, and ferry crossings to Samal Island.

Carmen is a serene coastal and agricultural municipality nestled between Panabo City and Tagum City along the Davao Gulf in Davao del Norte.

Known for its expansive mango orchards, lush rice paddies, and winding river estuaries, Carmen offers a peaceful countryside escape just 40 minutes from Davao City. Birdwatchers and eco-travelers visit the Ising Wetlands and coastal mangrove boardwalks at sunrise.

Whether stopping for fresh tropical fruit stands along the highway or using Carmen as a quiet base for Davao del Norte roadtrips, travelers experience authentic rural Mindanao warmth.

Just a 10-minute roll-on/roll-off barge from Sasa Wharf or a quick boat ride from Sta. Ana Wharf in Davao City, the Island Garden City of Samal (IGaCoS) is the premier island playground of Region XI.

The island stretches across lush limestone ridges and palm-lined coves—from the luxury overwater villas of Pearl Farm Beach Resort and Malipano Island in the south to the multi-tiered jungle cascades of Hagimit Falls and the Guinness-listed Monfort Bat Sanctuary in Babak.

Divers and snorkelers flock to Samal's crystal-clear reefs, Taklobo Giant Clam Sanctuary, and vibrant marine gardens, making it an essential multi-day stop on any Davao itinerary.

Tucked off the southwestern tip of Samal Island, Talikud Island rewards travelers who venture slightly farther with untouched powdery white beaches and thriving coral reefs.

Highlights include the shaded coconut groves of Isla Reta, the calm turquoise lagoon of Babu Santa Beach, and the Coral Garden Marine Park—one of the richest snorkeling and drift-diving sites in the Davao Gulf.

Day-trippers typically depart from Sta. Ana Wharf in Davao City or Kaputian Beach on Samal by outrigger pumpboat, spending the day swimming among sea turtles, giant clams, and rainbow-colored reef fish.

Perched on the Pacific rim of Mindanao in Davao Oriental, Mati City is a sun-soaked coastal paradise famous for the 7-kilometer crescent of Dahican Beach.

Dahican's rolling Pacific swells attract surfers and skimboarders from across the Philippines, while its protected sandy shore serves as a vital nesting sanctuary for endangered Hawksbill and Olive Ridley sea turtles (pawikan).

Just outside town, travelers stop at the Badas Point overlook to photograph the iconic Sleeping Dinosaur peninsula, explore the Subangan Museum's massive sperm whale skeleton, or take an ultralight flight soaring above Pujada Bay.

Designated as one of the Most Beautiful Bays in the World, Pujada Bay wraps around Mati City with calm, jewel-toned waters sheltered by dramatic coastal headlands.

Island-hopping boats depart from Mati Baywalk to reach Waniban Island's coconut-fringed white sand beach, the shifting tidal sandbars of Oak Island and Puting Bato, and vibrant shallow-water coral reefs.

With minimal crowds and fresh kinilaw (Mindanao ceviche) lunches prepared right on the beach, Pujada Bay offers a tranquil counterpoint to the surf energy of nearby Dahican Beach.

Located 3,000 feet above sea level in Toril, Davao City, Eden Nature Park & Resort is an 80-hectare mountain sanctuary carved out of a once-logged hillside into a thriving pine and rainforest reserve.

Cool mountain breezes carry the scent of pine needles as guests stroll through the Amphitheater, Butterfly Garden, Indiana Jones trail, and organic hydroponic vegetable gardens. Thrill-seekers can ride the Skycycle—pedaling a suspended bicycle 60 feet above the forest canopy—or soar on the Skyrider zipline.

Just 45 minutes from downtown Davao City, Eden is ideal for crisp morning coffee, farm-to-table buffets, and panoramic views overlooking the Davao Gulf.

Set in the cool, forested foothills of Baguio District in Davao City, Malagos is the ecological and culinary pride of the Davao highlands.

The Philippine Eagle Center protects and breeds the critically endangered Philippine Eagle (Pithecophaga jefferyi) within a lush 8-hectare rainforest habitat alongside hornbills, owls, and reptiles. Nearby, the Malagos Garden Resort houses the Philippines' first tree-to-bar Chocolate Museum, where visitors taste single-origin Davao cacao awarded globally.

Combine both stops with a visit to the Malagos Farmhouse for artisanal goat cheeses before heading back into the city.

Stretching along the scenic Bukidnon-Davao (Buda) Highway in Marilog District, this misty highland corridor sits over 1,200 meters above sea level and is affectionately called the 'Little Baguio of Davao.'

Morning fog drifts through tall Benguet pines, cozy A-frame mountain cabins, strawberry picking farms, and cliffside cafes like Pilgrim and Seagull Mountain Resort. Travelers can also visit Bemwa Farm for fresh highland produce or admire the cascading Epol Falls along the highway.

A 90-minute drive northwest from downtown Davao City, Buda is the region's favorite weekend escape for cool weather and stargazing.

Tucked in the lush mountains of Cateel in northern Davao Oriental, Aliwagwag Falls Eco-Park is widely hailed as the highest tiered waterfall in the Philippines.

Over 84 natural rock ledges form a towering 1,110-foot staircase of rushing whitewater framed by towering dipterocarp trees. Visitors cross a hanging bridge for dramatic frontal views, swim in cool emerald plunge pools at the base, and ride a 680-meter zipline directly over the cascading falls.

Paired with the coastal towns of Baganga and Boston, Cateel anchors the unforgettable northern Pacific loop of Davao Oriental.

At the dramatic southeasternmost tip of the Davao Peninsula in Gobernador Generoso, Cape San Agustin marks the meeting point of the Davao Gulf and the vast Celebes Sea.

Three historic lighthouses—including a century-old Spanish-era tower—stand guard above rugged limestone cliffs, pink-tinted Parola Beach, and the natural rock formation known as The Altar, where ocean swells crash dramatically against the shore.

The scenic coastal drive south from Mati City passes coconut groves, quiet fishing villages, and panoramic cliffside viewpoints.

Baganga along Davao Oriental's rugged Pacific coast is a hidden eco-adventure treasure chest.

Its centerpiece is Carolina Lake, a tranquil emerald-green brackish lagoon separated from the Pacific Ocean by a narrow strip of forest, ideal for kayaking and paddleboarding. Nearby, visitors explore the misty Curtain Falls, stroll along Sunrise Boulevard, and take boats out to San Victor Island and the Poo Sandbar.

Baganga's unspoiled coastline makes it a rewarding stopover on the Mati-to-Cateel Pacific highway.

city: Mt. Apo Natural Park & Lake Venado
country: Davao del Sur / Davao City • Region XI
description:
Towering at 2,954 meters above sea level, Mount Apo is the highest peak in the Philippines and an ASEAN Heritage Park straddling Davao del Sur and Davao City.

Trekkers ascend through mossy cloud forests, giant ferns, and steaming volcanic sulfur vents before reaching the iconic boulder face and the serene alpine mirror of Lake Venado. At sunrise from the summit crater, climbers are rewarded with sweeping views above a sea of clouds stretching from Davao Gulf to Cotabato.

Guided climbs via the Sta. Cruz, Kapatagan, or Bansalan trails typically span 2 to 3 days.

Nestled on the cool southern slopes of Mount Apo in Digos City, Kapatagan is a serene mountain plateau offering front-row views of the Philippines' tallest volcano without needing to summit.

Travelers wake up to crisp highland air at Lake Mirror and Mt. Apo Highland Resort, sip single-origin Mt. Apo Arabica coffee at hillside cafes, and explore Agong House and Camp Sabros ziplines.

Just 90 minutes south of Davao City, Kapatagan is a favorite retreat for glamping, photography, and cool-climate relaxation.

As the vibrant capital of Davao del Sur, Digos City sits along the western coast of Davao Gulf and serves as the gateway to Mount Apo and southern Mindanao.

Food lovers know Digos for its ultra-sweet carabao mangoes, bustling public market, and famed crispy lechon stalls. Along the coast, Dawis and Aplaya boardwalks offer sunset views across the gulf toward Samal and Davao City.

From Digos, scenic mountain roads climb directly up to the cool highland plateau of Kapatagan.

Just 35 minutes south of Davao City, Sta. Cruz blends rugged mountain adventure with calm coastal escapes.

Inland, Sta. Cruz is the classic jump-off point for Mt. Apo treks via the dramatic Tinikaran boulder trail. Along the coast in Barangay Bato, Passig Islet Aqua-Eco Park sits just offshore—a charming 1-hectare coral islet connected to the mainland by a wooden footbridge over clear blue water.

Families and road-trippers stop here for snorkeling, open-air cottages, and fresh grilled seafood.

Cradled in a lush mountain valley in Davao de Oro, Maragusan is a cool highland paradise known as the 'Summer Capital of Davao de Oro.'

Early risers hike or drive up to Haven's Peak and Sea of Clouds viewpoints to watch golden sunlight spill over mist-filled valleys. Throughout the municipality, towering waterfalls including Tagbibinta Falls, Pyalitan Falls, and Kanlawig Hot Springs invite refreshing afternoon dips.

About 3 hours northeast of Davao City via Tagum and Nabunturan, Maragusan is a must-visit for highland nature lovers.

Facing the calm northeastern waters of Davao Gulf, the coastal town of Mabini in Davao de Oro is the gateway to the Protected Landscape and Seascape of Kopiat and Lunod Islands.

A short 15-minute boat ride from Pindasan Wharf brings visitors to Kopiat Island's powdery white-sand shores, shaded coconut groves, and sea turtle nesting beaches. Neighboring Dusit Thani Lubi Plantation Resort on Pindasan Island offers upscale resort amenities overlooking the gulf.

Mabini is an easy 2-hour coastal drive from Davao City.

Located in northern Davao de Oro, Monkayo is celebrated for the dramatic multi-tiered curtain of Awao Falls and the misty mountain ridges of Mt. Diwata.

Awao Falls cascades down a broad, mossy rock amphitheater surrounded by thick tropical forest, offering cool natural swimming pools and bamboo picnic huts. Nearby caves and river valleys make Monkayo a rewarding eco-tourism stop along the Agusan-Davao highway.

Nabunturan, the capital of Davao de Oro, is famed for the therapeutic geothermal waters of Mainit Hot Springs Protected Landscape.

Naturally heated sulfur springs cascade down limestone terraces into cool mountain streams, creating warm-and-cold natural spa pools under a dense rainforest canopy. Visitors also explore the Toyozu Falls and nearby limestone caves before continuing to Maragusan.

Strategically positioned just 30 minutes north of Davao City, Panabo City is known as the Banana Capital of the Philippines and a lively coastal hub of Davao del Norte.

Highlights include the Panabo Mariculture Park's floating seafood restaurants, coastal mangrove eco-parks, and historical tunnels from World War II. Its proximity to Davao City makes it an easy stop along the northbound highway toward Tagum and Davao de Oro.

Tucked in the northern karst hills of Davao del Norte, Kapalong is Mindanao's premier spelunking destination.

Home to over 30 mapped limestone caverns—including Okbot Cave, Alcoba Cave, and the Suaon Underground River—Kapalong invites adventurous travelers to wade through subterranean streams and marvel at cathedral-like stalactite chambers surrounded by lush upland forest.

At the dramatic southernmost frontier of the Davao Region in Davao Occidental, the twin volcanic islands of Balut and Sarangani rise from the Celebes Sea.

Balut Island is home to the steaming geothermal pools of Sabang Hot Springs, the dormant Mt. Balut crater lake, and untouched white-sand coves at Tuke Maklang. Neighboring Sarangani Island offers secluded beaches, rich coral drop-offs, and warm island hospitality far off the beaten path.
